job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today we are discussing India's lifelines. Rohan, what do you think about our transport network? Rohan: I believe the Golden Quadrilateral is the most important, as it connects all major state capitals to boost trade. Teacher: Actually, Rohan, it links major industrial, agricultural, and cultural hubs, not every state capital. Priya, what about pipelines? Priya: I think pipelines are only used to transport water for drinking. Teacher: That is a common mistake; they are essential for transporting crude oil, petroleum, and natural gas from refineries to inland locations. Priya: What about using our rivers for large ships to increase trade? Teacher: Not all rivers are navigable for large ships due to depth and seasonal flow. Regarding trade, a country is considered economically healthy when its exports exceed its imports, creating a favorable balance of trade, rather than just keeping them equal. It is about the value of goods exchanged. Rohan: So, it is not just about moving water or balancing numbers? Teacher: Exactly. It is about strategic connectivity and the value of what we trade globally.

items.evidence: Actually, Rohan, it links major industrial, agricultural, and cultural hubs, not every state capital.
items.q: Rohan says the Golden Quadrilateral joins every state capital. What does the teacher's correction show?
options: It joins major economic hubs, not all capitals
It joins only the four biggest state capitals
It joins all capitals but only for trade
It joins railway stations of the main cities
items.explain: The teacher said it links major industrial, agricultural and cultural hubs, not every state capital.

wrong.why: swaps one wrong limit for another, still thinking it is about capitals
thinks it connects all state capitals
thinks it is a railway network

items.evidence: That is a common mistake; they are essential for transporting crude oil, petroleum, and natural gas from refineries to inland locations.
items.q: A refinery on the coast must send petroleum to a distant inland city. What would pipelines do here?
options: Carry the petroleum from the refinery inland
Carry only drinking water to the city
Carry the petroleum only within the refinery
Carry the petroleum back from inland cities
items.explain: Pipelines carry crude oil, petroleum and natural gas from refineries to inland locations, not only water.

wrong.why: thinks pipelines are only used inside the plant
reverses the direction of the flow

items.evidence: Not all rivers are navigable for large ships due to depth and seasonal flow.
items.q: Why can a trader not send large ships along every river to boost trade?
options: Some rivers are too shallow or seasonal
Large ships are banned on most rivers
Rivers only flow near the Golden Quadrilateral
Rivers are used only for carrying water
items.explain: Not all rivers are navigable for large ships because of their depth and seasonal flow.

wrong.why: invents a rule not in the passage
mixes up rivers with the Golden Quadrilateral network
thinks water transport means only carrying water

items.evidence: Regarding trade, a country is considered economically healthy when its exports exceed its imports, creating a favorable balance of trade, rather than just keeping them equal.
items.q: Which country is in the healthiest trade position, going by the teacher's idea?
options: One selling goods worth more than it buys
One buying goods worth the same as it sells
One buying goods worth more than it sells
One buying and selling the same goods daily
items.explain: A country is healthy when exports exceed imports, giving a favourable balance of trade, not equal trade.

wrong.why: thinks equal exports and imports is best
thinks matching trade of the same goods means health
